newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak urges more Middle East peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak urges more Middle East peace talks.

text.p: Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak said on Tuesday Israel should continue peace talks with Palestinians despite two suicide bombings in Jerusalem last week because peace was the only way to avoid further "terrorism".

Mubarak also told reporters after talks with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy that it was "dangerous" to weaken Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's position. He said Arafat was not "powerful enough" to implement the tough measures Israel demanded of him.

Levy's talks with Mubarak and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa came amid a growing crisis in Middle East peace efforts that were dealt a further blow when two suicide bombers killed 13 people in a west Jerusalem market.
Mubarak said Israeli leaders should take a page out of former Labour prime minister Yitzhak Rabin's book by resuming peace talks with the Palestinians despite such attacks.

"I remember when Mr. Rabin was in power, they may get offended when I say that, but this is a good example. When there was an explosion or terrorist action in Tel Aviv, right away after that he (Rabin) said 'I am going to continue negotiations for peace," Mubarak told reporters.

"It's a very wise statement because the only way to avoid terrorism and to avoid violence is to go through the peace process, because this terroristic action may be to hinder progress in the peace process," he added.
Talks between Israel and the Palestinians collapsed in March after Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Levy and Palestinian negotiator Nabil Shaath agreed last week that joint Israeli-PLO committees would renew talks on outstanding issues from a 1995 peace deal.

But after the suicide bombing Israel suspended peace talks and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, disrupting Palestinian trade and preventing tens of thousands of Arab workers from reaching their jobs in the Jewish state.
It also threatened to re-enter Palestinian self-rule areas to fight militants if Arafat did not clamp down on Islamic militants.
Israel said on Tuesday that Arafat had yet to act against anti-Israeli militants six days after the suicide bombings.
"Without these demands being met, the peace process between them and us is in danger," Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told reporters at an army induction base in Tel Aviv.
Mubarak said Arafat had limited power to act against such militants and that Israeli measures against Palestinians weakened him further.

"Arafat is not that powerful (a) leader in this terrible area to take tough measures, bearing in mind that he is being weakened every now and then by some measures taken by the Israelis," Mubarak said.
"Weakening the position of Arafat is very, very dangerous in the peace process. Whether somebody understands or doesn't understand it's very important to keep him in power," he added.

Mubarak said he told Levy that "punishing the Palestinians -- no food, no medicine -- is very dangerous and may have very negative reactions and I ask them to find a quick solution to the present situation in what will be next for the peace."

Asked if he had any formula to restart the peace process, Mubarak said: "At least to find the solution to the present situation now, because the present situation may help much more terrorism. This is our fear. Secondly we have to slow down the so-called settlements and these things."

Mubarak said he also told Levy that Israel should reopen the border post between Egypt and the Palestinian self-rule areas in order to ease the plight of about 500 Palestinians stuck on the Egyptian side.
